summary: US-023c2: Catalog emits performance.published schema 5 for rule-enabled maps
description:
**Created during TKT-180's second ai-review**, which found ADR-041's rollout section self-contradictory: it argued that consumer-before-producer ordering *"is only expressible as separate merges"* and then assigned both inventory's schema-5 arm and catalog's emission to TKT-181.

**A shared merge does not order a deployment.** Catalog and inventory start independently, so one PR carrying both does not guarantee inventory is running first. If catalog emits while an old inventory replica is still up, that replica **quarantines the event, acks it, and latches unready** — and deploying the capable binary does **not** repair it. Quarantined originals were acked, so recovery is `reprocess-quarantine` **plus a restart**, by an operator. Newly published performances would have no inventory pool until someone notices.

So the producer gets its own revision.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Catalog emits `performance.published` **schema 5** for a seated performance whose bound seat-map version has `orphan_prevention_enabled` true, carrying the exact `seat_map_id` and the flag.
- [ ] A rule-**off** seated map still emits **schema 4**, byte-identical to today's golden. A GA performance is untouched.
- [ ] The schema-5 payload has its own golden, and the schema-4 golden is unchanged in the same commit — the pair is what proves the fork rather than a rewrite.
- [ ] The event carries the version the performance is bound to, never the family's current version (ADR-029) — a test seats a performance against v1, publishes v2 with a different setting, and asserts the emitted event still describes v1.
- [ ] Smoke proves an enabled map publishes at schema 5 and provisions an inventory pool **with** its adjacency projection (TKT-181's work, exercised end to end here for the first time).

### Two additions from TKT-180's third ai-review

**1. This ships AFTER the rule (TKT-182), not before it.** The original order put emission before enforcement, which opens a window where organizers have enabled the rule, inventory has recorded the flag and the projection, and buyers can still strand seats — silently, for the length of a deployment, on a revenue rule someone deliberately turned on. TKT-182 is dormant until a schema-5 pool exists, so shipping it first costs nothing.

**2. Performances already published against an enabled map must be re-emitted, and nothing else in the sequence does it.** TKT-179 shipped the setting before this ticket ships the transport, so a performance can be published against a rule-enabled map **today**: catalog emits it at schema 4, sets `event_emitted_at`, and never emits it again — re-POSTing publish is idempotent and will not re-fire. Inventory provisions an ordinary seated pool with no flag and no adjacency, and it stays that way for ever while the back office insists the rule is on.

- [ ] A correction wave re-emits `performance.published` at schema 5 for every published performance bound to a rule-enabled map version, under a **fresh event identity** — the existing `reemit-policies` path uses fixed correction ids that may already be in `consumed_events`, where a replay is a silent no-op.
- [ ] Inventory's schema-5 handler **upgrades an existing seated pool** — attaching the flag and projection to a pool that already exists — rather than assuming it only ever provisions new ones. (This may require an amendment to TKT-181's scope; check before starting.)
- [ ] The wave is replay-safe and idempotent, proven by running it twice.
- [ ] A test seeds a performance published against an enabled map *before* the wave and asserts it ends up with flag and projection.

**Deploy note:** TKT-181's inventory and TKT-182's rule must both be fully rolled out before this is enabled. That ordering is the whole reason this ticket exists.

Quality gates: `make check` green; both goldens; smoke.

reference.summary: The rollout rule this ticket enforces

governingAdrs.why: The producer half of the bump, and the reason it is a separate revision: bump on consumer semantics, and never emit a variant before every consumer accepts it.
The event must name the exact bound version, never the family's current one — resolving the family would describe a map the pool is not seated against.
Quarantine and readiness behaviour is what makes a premature emission expensive: quarantined originals are acked and recovery is manual.
